description: Two independent trigger sequencers on one panel: an upper one of 4 or 8 steps and a lower one of 8 or 16, each step latched on or off.

params.text: Chooses 4 or 8 steps for the upper sequencer.
Reverses the direction the upper sequencer runs in.
Latches that step of the upper sequencer on or off; a trigger comes out when the playhead lands on a step that is on.
Chooses 8 or 16 steps for the lower sequencer.
Reverses the direction the lower sequencer runs in.
Latches that step of the lower sequencer on or off; a trigger comes out when the playhead lands on a step that is on.

inputs.text: A rising edge past 1V moves the upper sequencer on one step, or back one step while its reverse switch is on.
A rising edge past 1V flips the upper sequencer between 4 and 8 steps, moving the panel switch with it.
A rising edge past 1V flips the upper sequencer's reverse switch, moving the panel switch with it.
A rising edge past 1V moves the lower sequencer on one step, or back one step while its reverse switch is on.
A rising edge past 1V flips the lower sequencer between 8 and 16 steps, moving the panel switch with it.
A rising edge past 1V flips the lower sequencer's reverse switch, moving the panel switch with it.

outputs.text: A 10V pulse 1ms long each time the upper sequencer's playhead lands on a step that is latched on.
A 10V pulse 1ms long each time the lower sequencer's playhead lands on a step that is latched on.

notes: There is no reset jack. Reset arrives only from a TL_Reseter placed directly to the left or the right, whose A half resets the upper sequencer and B half the lower one.
A reset puts the playhead at the first step, or at the last step while that sequencer is reversed.
Shortening a sequencer does not move the playhead. If it was on a step beyond the new length it stays there until the next clock brings it back inside.
The step pattern is held in the switch positions and so survives a patch save, but the playhead position does not: both sequencers start again from step 1 on load.
